solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Take out one side of car after collision

indicators.note: 'after' places the side piece second, behind the crash word

blocks.note: a bump is a minor collision
the off side of a car is the side nearest the middle of the road

explanation.surface: A driver loses a whole flank of the car in a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the pieces backwards: the side comes 'after' the collision, so the crash word goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for murdering someone, as gangsters say of a rival.

clue.text: Kicking ball a bit, idler pocketed sports equipment

indicators.note: kicking things about scatters them, so these letters land in a new order

blocks.note: the thirteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A lazy player toys with a ball and somehow sinks it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pocketed' sounds like part of the wordplay but simply links, and nods to the pockets of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A billiard table is the cloth-covered surface with pockets on which billiards and snooker are played.

clue.text: Indistinct sounds from doctor wearing slippers

indicators.note: whoever wears something has it around them, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: mules are backless slippers
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor in carpet slippers shuffles about muttering.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumbles are words spoken too quietly or unclearly to make out, a plural noun like the clue's sounds.

clue.text: Haven now out of bounds in its current state

indicators.note: the edges of the word are put out of play, keeping only its centre

blocks.note: the middle letter once the outer pair is gone
'as is' means unchanged, in the condition it now is

explanation.surface: A refuge that is closed to visitors but otherwise left exactly as it stands.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot in a desert, and figuratively any refuge or place of calm.

clue.text: Tire European staff

blocks.note: to flag is to grow tired
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: Reads as an instruction to wear out a member of staff from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff is a pole, and a flagpole is the staff from which a flag flies.

clue.text: Malign US agent sent back a third note

indicators.note: something sent back returns the way it came, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: a Fed is an FBI agent in American slang
taken as written
me (mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A nasty American agent is returned with a coded musical message.
explanation.definitionFit: To malign someone is to speak ill of them, and to defame is to damage a reputation the same way.

clue.text: Go up into sanctum and fall

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters run from the bottom back to the top
one thing put into another sits inside it

blocks.note: a den is a private retreat, one's sanctum
to go is a euphemism for urinating

explanation.surface: A worshipper climbs into the holy of holies and then tumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair because a voice or note that falls in pitch is said to deepen.
explanation.definitionFit: When a sound falls in pitch it becomes lower, which is to deepen; both are intransitive verbs.

clue.text: Previous award I received, after warning of course

indicators.note: something received is taken in and held

blocks.note: golfers shout fore on a golf course to warn of a ball in flight
a gong is slang for a medal or honour
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recalls an earlier prize collected after being cautioned during a course.
explanation.walkthrough: Of course really means 'on a golf course'.
explanation.definitionFit: Foregoing means already mentioned or happening before, a synonym of previous.

clue.text: Gigantic insect covering a tiny distance

indicators.note: a thing that covers another wraps around it

blocks.note: a moth is a winged insect
taken as written
MM, a millimetre, is a very short length

explanation.surface: A paradox: a huge insect that can only cross a minute span.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammoth works as an adjective for anything of enormous size, from the extinct elephant.

clue.text: Deposit fruit and veg, by the sound of it

indicators.note: we are told to judge by what we hear, not by the spelling

blocks.note: limes are citrus fruit
kale is a leafy green vegetable; with the S it sounds like this

explanation.surface: A greengrocer drops off a delivery of produce.
explanation.walkthrough: Say limes kale quickly and you hear the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Limescale is the chalky deposit left by hard water inside kettles and pipes.

clue.text: Plays piano later than expected in concert series

indicators.note: something arriving late turns up further along than its usual place

blocks.note: the Proms are the BBC's summer series of London concerts
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A pianist turns up late during a run of concerts.
explanation.walkthrough: The P that normally opens the concert word moves further along, appearing later than expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Romps are boisterous games or frolics, so as a verb romps means plays energetically.

clue.text: Controlled plan's beneath grand editor

blocks.note: super means excellent, grand
to intend is to plan
ed is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor's grand scheme has been reined in.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'beneath' means below, so the plan sits under the grand word.
explanation.definitionFit: To superintend is to oversee or manage, so superintended means directed or controlled.

clue.text: Fateful day during which learner fritters time away

indicators.note: something happening during a period lies inside it

blocks.note: the Ides of March, when Caesar was killed
L for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: On a fateful date, a learner wastes the hours.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to waste time doing nothing, a verb in the same third-person form as fritters.

clue.text: Noble band, all of similar age

blocks.note: a peer is a nobleman
a band is a group

explanation.surface: A troupe of aristocrats who are all contemporaries.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer group is a set of people of roughly the same age or status, described rather than named.

clue.text: Roguish head of syndicate around in convention

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
the pieces are placed inside the gathering

blocks.note: a rally is a mass meeting or convention
its opening letter
ca, circa, means around

explanation.surface: A shady crime boss mingles at a conference.
explanation.definitionFit: Rascally means behaving like a rascal, mischievous or dishonest, the same as roguish.

clue.text: Genuine article in auction, not old, reproduced

indicators.note: the article is placed inside the sale word
O, short for old, is taken away
something reproduced is made anew, here in a different letter order

blocks.note: the is the definite article
taken as written before losing a letter

explanation.surface: A sale-room piece turns out to be a modern copy, ironically.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a fake at auction, yet the answer means the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Authentic and genuine are synonyms: real, not forged.

clue.text: Perish alongside retreating army corps

indicators.note: troops retreating go backwards, so the letters run right to left

blocks.note: with means alongside, together
RE, the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: Soldiers die as their unit falls back.
explanation.definitionFit: To wither is to shrivel and die, as plants do, so it fits perish as a verb.

clue.text: Appropriate work left in course of move

indicators.note: things occurring in the course of something lie inside it

blocks.note: to shift is to move
op, opus, is a work
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Some suitable work was left behind during a house move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to take.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate is to take something for oneself; shoplifting is stealing from a store.

clue.text: Time left before end of journey for cardinal

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: T is the symbol for time
went is the past of go, i.e. left
its final letter

explanation.surface: A churchman sets off before his trip is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardinal is not the churchman but a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty is a cardinal number, one used for counting rather than ordering.

clue.text: Fire England's opening pair so close to game

indicators.note: the opening pair means the first two letters
the close of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: the first two letters
thus means so, therefore
its last letter

explanation.surface: England's opening batsmen are dismissed, nearly ending the match.
explanation.walkthrough: Fire is the verb to excite or inspire, not a sacking or a bowler's firing out.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone up is to stir their excitement, much as to enthuse is to fill with eagerness.

clue.text: Hide product from diminished ruler with little experience

indicators.note: made smaller by losing its last letter

blocks.note: a shah was the ruler of Iran
green means inexperienced

explanation.surface: A deposed monarch with no experience goes into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: Hide is the noun, an animal skin, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Shagreen is untanned leather with a rough grainy surface, a product made from animal hide.

clue.text: Great line from Eastern queen on upcoming schedule

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: E for Eastern
Qu is an abbreviation for queen
a rota is a schedule of duties

explanation.surface: An oriental monarch delivers a memorable remark about her forthcoming timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The equator is a great circle, the longest line of latitude around the Earth.

clue.text: Denounce Charlie dipping into exotic sauce

indicators.note: something exotic is strange, so these letters come out unfamiliar
dipping into something goes inside it

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone called Charlie dunks food into a spicy dip.
explanation.definitionFit: To accuse and to denounce both mean to charge someone publicly with wrongdoing.

clue.text: Merest trace of canker in flatter flower

indicators.note: the smallest trace of a word is just its first letter
one piece placed inside another

blocks.note: to butter up is to flatter
its first letter

explanation.surface: A gardener spots a slight blight in an otherwise perfect bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Flatter looks like an adjective, more level, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttercup is a common yellow wild flower.

clue.text: Car's tremendous feat when energy's added

indicators.note: something added is tacked on at the end, so this piece comes last

blocks.note: a coup is a brilliant achievement
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A car does something amazing once given a power boost.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupe is a two-door car with a fixed roof.

clue.text: Envy beastly doctor in joint practice?

blocks.note: co- is the prefix meaning joint, as in a shared practice
a vet is a doctor for animals

explanation.surface: Jealousy of an animal doctor within a shared surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsy: a vet in a joint practice would be a co-vet.
explanation.definitionFit: To covet is to desire what another has, which is to envy them.

clue.text: Crow by last month on verge of extinction

indicators.note: the verge is the edge, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: its first letter
x is the multiplication sign, read as by, as in 3 by 4
ult., ultimo, means of last month in old letter style

explanation.surface: A bird species was last seen a month ago, close to dying out.
explanation.walkthrough: Crow is the verb, to gloat, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to boast triumphantly, which is to exult.

clue.text: Divine nut cracked — that's not called for

indicators.note: something cracked is broken up, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A holy crank goes mad, which was quite unnecessary.
explanation.definitionFit: Uninvited means not asked for or welcome, as with an unrequested remark.

clue.text: Second copper stopping payment for grass

indicators.note: something that stops a gap fills it, sitting inside

blocks.note: a fee is a payment
S for second
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A second police officer blocks a payment to an informer.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper and grass both suggest police and informers; here grass is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Fescue is a genus of grass widely used for lawns and pasture.

clue.text: Did coach change route within Thailand's borders?

indicators.note: a word's borders are its first and last letters
to change the word is to rearrange its letters
one part goes inside the other

blocks.note: its first and last letters
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A tour coach driver alters the route inside Thailand.
explanation.walkthrough: Coach is the verb, to teach, not a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: To tutor is to coach or teach, so tutored matches the past tense did coach.
